subject: Staffing consequence matrix — vote and actions for QBR
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Staffing consequence matrix — vote and actions for QBR

Team —

As we close the OKR check-ins and lock the QBR narrative, we need a definitive headcount decision set that ties to the OKR-impact matrix. I attached the latest "headcount_matrix_v3.xlsx" with two tabs: "Consequence Matrix" and "Req Decision Log." Please review and vote on the proposals below by EOD Wed (Nov 18):

Proposals (high level):
- Freeze: hold all non-customer-facing IC reqs except for critical infra and security (proposed freeze scope in matrix).
- Backfill priority: Dedicated runtime and KV-cache reliability engineers (2 FTE each) — these are marked P0 in the matrix.
- Contractors: authorize up to 3 contractor slots for QA/bug triage through Q1 while hiring proceeds.

Quick asks from each of you:
1) Approve/Reject the freeze as scoped (yes/no).
2) Confirm which req IDs you think are truly P0 and must be staffed before Q1.
3) Any procurement constraints we should surface to Finance (Vanessa) now?

Attachments: [attachment: headcount_matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Why this matters: the matrix maps each req to OKR impact, customer risk, and unit-cost delta. We need a one-line rationale in the log for anything we keep open. I will consolidate votes and produce a final decision doc for the QBR packet.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Director, People Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staffing consequence matrix — vote and actions for QBR

+1 to Tessa's approach. A few details from Eng perspective:

- I support freezing non-customer-facing product growth ICs. We should explicitly exempt runtime reliability work — the matrix already flags these but make them non-negotiable P0.
- For Dedicated runtime backfills: drop to 1 FTE immediate hire and 1 contractor for the interim if hiring timeline slips. That reduces near-term capex while protecting availability.
- Please add a "sequence-risk" column to the matrix (how much delay cascades to downstream OKRs) — I'll send a tiny CSV to merge.

On procurement: if we go contractor-first for the short term, we will need a rapid vendor onboarding path. Tagging our procurement partner (Ava Consulting) in the thread is fine — they can advise on SOW language.

On quoting Tessa:
> Freeze: hold all non-customer-facing IC reqs except for critical infra and security (proposed freeze scope in matrix).

I agree. Marking my vote: Approve freeze (with exceptions above). I will list the req-IDs I care about by EOB today.

—Jonas
VP, Product & Platform

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staffing consequence matrix — vote and actions for QBR

Thanks — quick engineering addendum.

- Req IDs I believe must remain open: RQ-1183 (Dedicated Serving Infra), RQ-1197 (KV-cache stability), RQ-1220 (SRE coverage for EU region). These are tied to SLAs in existing contracts; we risk SLA breaches if we delay.
- For the Dedicated Serving Infra req (RQ-1183), we should consider hiring a senior engineer + one mid-level instead of two juniors. That will expedite ramp and reduce debugging cycles.
- I've attached a procurement estimate for the contractor stopgap and the FTE delta (procurement_estimate.pdf).

On temporary contractors: we should limit them to triage and bursts; no long-term core-system ownership. Vendor ops (ContractorOps) has capacity and can start within 10 business days if procurement clears SOW.

> On procurement: if we go contractor-first for the short term, we will need a rapid vendor onboarding path.

Agree — I'll coordinate with Ava Consulting to draft SOW language for a 90-day engagement.

-Markus
Head of Engineering, Serving Runtime
[attachment: procurement_estimate.pdf (pdf)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staffing consequence matrix — vote and actions for QBR

Team —

Summary decision (consolidated):
- Freeze approved for all non-customer-facing growth IC reqs EXCEPT the following approved exceptions (we will greenlight these reqs in the req_approval_log.csv and push for immediate start):
  * RQ-1183 (Dedicated Serving Infra) — approved (hire senior + mid).
  * RQ-1197 (KV-cache stability) — approved (1 FTE).
  * RQ-1220 (SRE EU) — approved (regional compliance risk).
- Contractors: approved up to 3 contractor slots for short-term triage; procurement to prioritize ContractorOps on a 90-day SOW.
- Financial guardrails: hiring manager to provide 6-month run-rate estimate for each approved req within 48 hours. If run-rate > $240k/year, escalate to Finance execs for sign-off.

Follow-ups & links: I updated the decision column in the attached req_approval_log.csv and uploaded the signed addendum to DocuSign (DocuSign:4f3a9b-addendum). Please ensure that all kept reqs include a one-line rationale for the QBR packet.

Attachments: [attachment: req_approval_log.csv (csv), attachment: headcount_matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

I'll convert this outcome into a one-pager for the QBR slide deck and circulate before Thurs EOD. Thanks for quick turns.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Finance Business Partner, People & GTM
Redwood Inference
